Basic Check: 1. Check the Ethernet cable or make sure Wi-Fi is turned on.
2. Run ipconfig /all and check the IPv4 address, Default Gateway and DNS Servers.
3. Run ping 127.0.0.1 to check the local TCP/IP stack.
1. Ethernet or Wi-Fi connection does not: The computer may not be connected to the local network.
Check if the Ethernet cable is connected correctly.
Try another Ethernet cable or network port if possible.
If you use Wi-Fi, make sure Wi-Fi is turned on.
Make sure Airplane mode is off.
Check the network adapter in Device Manager.
2. ipconfig shows a wrong or missing net: Check the IPv4 address, Default Gateway and DNS Servers.
If the IPv4 address starts with 169.254, the computer probably did not receive an address from DHCP.
Check the Ethernet or Wi-Fi connection.
Run ipconfig /all again and check the new configuration.
3. ping 127.0.0.1 does not work: This may mean there is a problem with the local TCP/IP stack.
Check the network adapter in Device Manager.
Try disabling and enabling the network adapter.
If the problem continues, the TCP/IP configuration may need further repair.
4. Ping to your own IPv4 address does no: The network adapter or local IP configuration may not be working correctly.
Run ipconfig /all and check the IPv4 address.
Disable and enable the network adapter.
Check the network adapter in Device Manager.
Restart the computer and test again.
5. Ping to the Default Gateway does not: The computer cannot communicate correctly with the local network gateway.
Check the Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi connection.
Run ipconfig /all and check the IPv4 address, Subnet Mask and Default Gateway.
Run ipconfig /renew if the computer uses DHCP.
Check if another device can reach the same Default Gateway.
6. Default Gateway works, but ping 8.8.8: The local network probably works, but the computer cannot reach the Internet.
Check if other users have Internet access.
If many users have the same problem, the router, firewall or ISP may be the cause.
Escalate the problem if it affects more than one computer.
7. ping 8.8.8.8 works, but ping google.c: The Internet connection probably works, but DNS may not be working.
Run ipconfig /all and check the DNS Servers.
8. nslookup google.com does not work: The DNS server may not be responding or the DNS configuration may be wrong.
Run ipconfig /all and check the DNS Servers.
Check if the DNS server address looks correct.
If other users have the same DNS problem, escalate it to the network administrator.
